title: Policy Decision Path Visualizer: interactive preview for region-tier-fallback rules
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Build an interactive Decision Path Visualizer in the Console policy editor that lets customers author and validate complex routing rules (region selection, tier routing, fallback model variants) and immediately see why a given request would route the way it does. Goal: reduce misconfigurations, speed up on-boarding for Dedicated/Private customers, and surface safe fallback suggestions before policies reach production.

Scope: visualizer canvas + step-through simulator, rule explainability (human-readable reasons and token-cost/latency estimates), preview mode with test traces and synthetic workloads, linter warnings for common pitfalls (cascading fallbacks, unavailable region tiers), and an exportable scenario runbook for SREs. This ticket covers PM & design acceptance criteria, API surface for the simulator, and Console wiring; engineering implementation split into ENG subtasks.

Out-of-scope for this ticket: runtime execution changes, deep kernel-level optimizations, or billing integration (handled in separate workstreams).
acceptance_criteria: Visualizer renders a decision graph for a given policy with nodes for region, tier, and model-variant conditions
Users can simulate a single request and a batch of synthetic requests; visualizer highlights the matched path and the fallback sequence
Each node shows rationale text, estimated 95th pct latency and per-token cost delta (derived from model profiles), and recent telemetry link
Policy linter surfaces at least five common errors (unreachable branches, circular fallbacks, ambiguous conditions) with suggested fixes
Preview mode supports toggling region availability and capacity to validate failover behavior
Export button generates a human-readable scenario runbook (markdown) and a JSON snapshot of the evaluated policy
Design sign-off (Figma) and a minimal Console integration prototype implemented behind a feature flag
End-to-end manual QA checklist passes on staging including canary failover simulation
